copy_pick.why: Its 'carcass' headline wears the nature-documentary voice best, 'missile fundraiser' is the day's one sharp line, it avoids C1's closer that echoes yesterday's 'nobody seems to be steering it' and C2's list-like ending, and its driver is the fullest real-story account of the heist, though all three

doom.driver: The $6.3 Billion Binance Hack Was Pulled Off in Just 20 Minutes. Multiple crypto-tracing firms say notorious North Korean hackers TraderTraitor may be behind the largest digital heist in history—with billions of crypto likely gone for good.
doom.blurb: PYONGYANG'S PACK STRIPS A $6.3 BILLION CARCASS
doom.summary: Twenty minutes. That's how long North Korea-linked hackers reportedly needed to empty $6.3 billion from Binance, and The Guardian notes that crypto theft provides roughly half of Pyongyang's foreign currency, so this heist is effectively a missile fundraiser. Meanwhile, a backdoored Claude Code extension reached thousands of developer machines, a contractor's Claude agent wandered into the Pentagon, and the Iran war grinds on in the background as Hegseth reshuffles generals and Houthis lob strikes at Saudi Arabia. Even the Pope is asking everyone to disarm the robots.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Altman says OpenAI's flood of math discoveries won't stop, Google is now running Gemma in orbit, and an AI agent reportedly found its way into the Pentagon.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: A judge had to block DOJ threats against election workers four days before the midterms, while Poland's government deployed police in a standoff over its top court.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: The Iran war is still active and driving oil profits, Houthis may be getting Russian satellite help against Saudi Arabia, and 500 Patriots are headed to Ukraine.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Official Claude extensions were backdoored for about 12 hours, a reminder that AI developer tooling is now a prime attack surface, whatever the models themselves intend.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: The largest crypto heist in history quietly tops up a nuclear state's budget, and flesh-eating screwworms have now spread to a third US state.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Interior of a cramped phone-and-crypto exchange kiosk in Computer Village, Ikeja, Lagos, late at night. We stand inside, looking out through the open corrugated-metal shutter doorway at the street. Outside, a narrow dusty road is lit by one sodium streetlamp. A wall of stacked market stalls, tangled overhead power cables and a dead billboard silhouette stand against a sky of deep black, with only a thin blood-orange haze along the horizon. Cool tones are almost extinguished, and everything is blood orange against deep black. The only light rises from below, like volcanic underlighting. A cracked inverter battery box on the floor glows through its vents like lava seams. It throws long orange shadows up the plywood walls and across the ceiling. On a plastic stool in the middle of the room sits a lone young trader, drawn whole, with his shoulders slumped. He holds a cracked smartphone whose screen shows only a stalled circular loading spinner, lit from beneath in harsh orange. Behind him, a peeling sticker of the Binance gold diamond on the wall has faded to a dull burnt orange. Beside him on the counter are a hardware wallet, a thick rubber-banded brick of naira notes, and a cheap analog wall clock stopped at twenty past the hour. Through the doorway, a second whole figure, a customer, stands in silhouette on the street and stares at a dead phone. Dust drifts in the orange glow, and the deep black pooling in the corners makes the room feel sealed and airless.

minor: The seated trader is almost entirely a dark silhouette, so his face and hands can't be read. The arm and phone connect plausibly to his body.
The foot at the bottom of the stool is murky and blends into the floor.
The clock on the right wall shows hands at an odd angle and its numerals are tiny and faint. They read as marks, not legible text.
The banknote brick on the counter has a smudgy label or band that looks like pseudo-text, but it is small and dim.
The Binance diamond sticker is large and clean rather than peeling, which is a mild mismatch with the prompt.
The inverter box at lower left is cluttered and its details are hard to parse.
The standing customer outside is a silhouette with an ambiguous dead phone, and the street background is a noisy jumble of stalls.

dawn.driver: Type 2 diabetes breakthrough as 54% achieve remission in just 6 months.
dawn.summary: More than half of adults under 45 with type 2 diabetes reached remission within six months on a structured low-calorie diet and exercise program. The tools are a dinner plate and a pair of sneakers, a treatment that almost anyone can reach. Elsewhere, 83-year-old Dave Obelkevich is lacing up for his record 50th straight New York City Marathon, and two astronauts spent more than seven hours outside the space station installing a new solar array.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: A computer scientist broke a limit that had stood since 1996, giving reliable distance estimates across huge networks without losing speed.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Countries at the global nature talks reached a deal to put the effort to protect biodiversity back on track.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: At 83, Dave Obelkevich is heading for his 50th consecutive NYC Marathon, a family tradition and a record streak.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Chesapeake Bay researchers and residents are finding creative ways to rebuild oyster reefs that clean the water and shelter other species.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A new solar array installed on the space station puts it on track for up to 30% more power by November 5.

copy_pick.why: Candidate 2 avoids the recent 'X: that is the result' and 'That is a...' sentence shapes that Candidates 1 and 3 reuse, wears the sports-desk voice with a 'squad benches diabetes' headline, and lands the sharpest specific line ('a dinner plate and a pair of sneakers') with no bad news.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. WIDE AERIAL VIEW looking down at a 45-degree angle over a vast river valley on the edge of a Canadian prairie city, in clear balanced golden-yellow daylight and fresh green, with confident, steady warmth. The landscape dominates the frame. A broad river curves through lush green parkland and poplar groves, and a distant skyline sits hazy on the horizon. In the middle ground, a winding paved riverside trail is dotted with dozens of tiny young adults jogging, walking briskly and cycling in pairs and small groups, their shadows long on the grass. To the left, a bustling outdoor farmers market fills a gravel lot, with striped awnings over crates of oranges, leafy greens, tomatoes and peppers, and a thick, happy crowd carrying full cloth bags. To the right, an outdoor fitness area on the lawn has pull-up bars and weight benches, with a loose class of tiny figures lifting and stretching in unison. In the lower foreground, a small brick corner pharmacy with a green cross sign stands on a quiet street. Its queue is empty, its drive-through lane has a single parked car, and one pharmacist stands whole and idle in the doorway looking out at the busy trail. Warm gold light rakes across the treetops and the trail curves toward the horizon, suggesting an ongoing journey.

minor: The fitness lawn on the right has a few unclear dark shapes near the right edge (weight benches or dumbbells merging with figures), but they read as gym equipment at phone size.
Some figures in the fitness class and market crowd are tiny, simplified blobs with ambiguous limbs, which is acceptable at this distance.
The parked car sits tightly against the pharmacy's drive-through canopy post, so the two overlap a little, but they are still readable as separate objects.
A few cyclists on the trail merge with their bikes into small clumps, which is typical for this scale of pixel art.
